reason: The decisive clash was found and priced (boss inside the knee link: +3.06 gate, +2.95 held). The priced fix, though, is the VERIFIER's patch (knee points within 6.33 mm of pin a lifted 5.69 mm, a 60-deg ramp). No design model of it exists, and its other clashes are unchecked. The lifted knee eye was checked against the shell top (jams 6 -> 5) but not against the E strap, the cuff-knee bearing stack (MR63ZZ pairs on a pin a that is now 5.69 mm taller) or the pad. The T-nut flange was priced only at 0.00 in the as-modelled state. 17.46 is a price, not a built-and-checked stack.

The relay's spring is scored at its planned state, and nothing shows it can hold that state. The relay is a passive coordinate held by a constant-force spring at 0.063 N.m preload. That preload covers gravity only (1.5x the max opening torque). Neither the iglidur-on-Ti carriage friction under the pad's load nor the spring's hysteresis is in it, so the return to the zero dowel is not shown. The spring has no part number and no sampled envelope; the verifier estimates an ~8 mm coil about 15 mm off the skin. On 3 bench poses the relay has two feasible ranges (a history-dependent state, worth up to ~0.8 points), and the folded-side relays are one-sided: the spring cannot push the other way, and those poses are the deepest contacts (9.79, 6.07 mm). No R17 / dynamics judge run and no cuff-twist (G3) measurement for this design are on file.

reason: Every relayed pose rides exactly on the fold-margin floor. The least-phi relay solve turns the carriage only until the lead's gates pass, so all relayed taken poses (23 bench, 74 held) sit at a th margin of exactly 5.000 deg (minimum 5.000 over 395 bench and 933 held taken poses, 0 below 5). That is legal under the one-metric rule. But CLAUDE.md treats the stop margin as a design variable where a passive coordinate takes poses past the stop (optimum 9-12 deg on arm-parked-knee-4r), with 5 deg as the lower bound. Here the margin was not searched, and the user's 'red-team the feel near the edge' has not been done for the relay. Any carriage friction or stop tolerance (the verifier estimates ~0.07 deg for an m6 dowel) lands directly in the fold margin.

The optimum sits on the search box's floors, on the side toward the skin. rt_extra (the shell's lift over the clip-p90 skin) is at its box edge of 1.5, below the spec range of 2-3.5, and the ramp is at its 60-deg floor. The claim-bench probe at the spec's rt_extra 2.5 reads gate 15.26 against 14.40, so 0.86 of the pre-registered pass rested on the low shell. The skin-bulge check the claim doc asked the verifier for (the low shell at the arm's widest section) is in neither verifier report. This is a bound walking toward the skin rather than toward a singular posture; it costs no contact on either bench (shell samples 99.5 % in band), but the bench's skin is not a contracting biceps.
